title: Run the case set and record the result immutably
problem: Running the cases is only useful if the result survives the next change. A run that overwrites the previous one destroys the history the whole tool exists to keep, and a run that stops at the first exception loses every result after it.
context: Builds on the validated case set from the previous task. The target under evaluation is supplied by the caller; the harness does not know what it is.
impact: This record is the durable artifact every comparison, claim and review later depends on. It is the one thing in the system that must not be wrong.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A second run never modifies or replaces the first run's record. Both remain readable afterwards.
A target that raises on one case does not prevent the remaining cases from being run and recorded.
A case that could not be evaluated is recorded as errored, with the exception type and message, and is never recorded as a failure.
The record identifies the target well enough to distinguish two different targets, not merely two different runs.
The record is readable and interpretable without the tool that wrote it.
Automated tests cover a clean run, a run with an erroring case, and the immutability of a prior record across a second run. All pass at the submitted revision.
The learner explains what identifies a target, one rejected alternative, and how a reader would detect a record that was written by an interrupted run.

constraints: Standard library plus a test runner only.
Errored and failed must remain distinct at every layer, including any summary. Merging them for convenience fails AC-errored-distinct.
Do not push to a remote or open a pull request as part of this task.

scope.description: Execution loop and the durable artifact it produces.

investigation_areas: What makes a record immutable in practice on a normal filesystem
What identifies the target, and what a caller can honestly supply
Which exceptions belong to the case and which belong to the harness itself
testing_expectations: Run the project's own test suite. State the exact command in the design.
documentation_requirements: Document the run record format as a stable contract, naming which fields a reader may rely on.

next_task_preview.summary: Report which specific cases changed and in which direction, rather than whether the total went up.
